title: Machine-learning-guided experiments identify a high-power-factor PbSe:SnSb thermoelectric family
summary: A closed-loop error-correction learning workflow guided synthesis of PbSe alloyed with SnSb and documented a previously unexplored low-temperature thermoelectric family. At 300 K, the best tested composition, 2 wt% SnSb-doped PbSe, had a measured power factor above 850 µW mK⁻² and more than twice that of PbSe. Density-functional calculations attribute the modeled transport improvement to Sn/Sb interactions that reduce hole effective mass.
ai_technology: Closed-loop error-correction learning with a neural-network update to a prior materials-property model; composition representations compared included Magpie, Roost and CrabNet
organization: University of Toronto; King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

evidence.tested: A closed-loop error-correction learning workflow guided synthesis of PbSe alloyed with SnSb and documented a previously unexplored low-temperature thermoelectric family.
evidence.unknown: The result is specific to the tested powder-processing, composition and measurement protocol, including synthesis below 300 °C; it is not evidence of device-level or commercial performance. The reported mechanism for the increased power factor is supported by DFT calculations, not a direct measurement of carrier effective mass. The paper compares the 2 wt% composition with PbSe and reports more than 2× power factor at room temperature.
evidence.ai_role: A model trained on published experimental thermoelectric data ranked candidate compositions, and a dense neural-network error-correction model incorporated local experimental comparisons to adapt predictions to the authors’ synthesis and measurement conditions. Iterative model-guided experiments selected the PbSe:SnSb family and 2 wt% SnSb-doped PbSe for characterization. AI supplied composition down-selection and adaptive experiment guidance; the authors synthesized and measured the samples.
